audit_items.title: Does patricialize correctly create BranchNodes with 16 subnodes when keys have no shared prefix at the current level?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: PROP-0031 targets the EL Patricia Merkle Trie function 'patricialize' (go-ethereum), which creates 16-subnode BranchNodes for keys with no shared prefix at the current trie level. The code resolved during Phase 02c is BeaconState.HashTreeRoot in beacon-chain/state/state-native/state_trie.go (lines 897-910). This is a binary Merkle tree implementation using SSZ (Simple Serialize), not a hexadecimal Patricia trie. Prysm is a consensus client and does not implement the EL Patricia Trie at all. The component_note in the audit item explicitly flags this mismatch.

recomputeDirtyFields iterates over dirtyFields map — Go map iteration is non-deterministic but does not affect correctness because each field root update is independent
Property mismatch: EL Patricia Trie patricialize/BranchNode/16-subnode concept does not exist anywhere in the Prysm codebase
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: merkleLayers cache protected by b.lock (write lock in HashTreeRoot). initializeMerkleLayers short-circuits if len(b.merkleLayers) > 0. dirtyFields populated by setter methods via markFieldAsDirty under write lock. Cache is consistent for SSZ tree.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: HashTreeRoot acquires b.lock.Lock() (exclusive write lock), serializing concurrent calls. recomputeFieldTrie releases fTrieMutex before assigning newTrie to b.stateFieldLeaves but parent write lock is held, so no concurrent reader can access.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No exploit scenario can be constructed for PROP-0031 (patricialize BranchNode 16-subnode creation) against Prysm's BeaconState.HashTreeRoot because the EL Patricia Trie code does not exist in this codebase. Symbolic execution of HashTreeRoot confirms correctness of the SSZ binary Merkle tree.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: No counterexample found — target code (patricialize) does not exist in this codebase. The actual HashTreeRoot correctly uses exclusive write lock preventing any external state manipulation.
attack_scenarios: PROPERTY-MISMATCH: Any exploitation of patricialize BranchNode creation would target go-ethereum (the execution client), not Prysm

INCIDENTAL: If a setter modifies state without markFieldAsDirty (e.g., via direct pointer write to shared reference), recomputeDirtyFields would skip that field — but this requires privileged internal access
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing-dependent exploit possible for stated property. Write lock eliminates TOCTOU for Merkle root computation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the trie root computation independent of trie._data.items() iteration order?

Go map iteration in recomputeDirtyFields is order-independent because each field's root update only affects its own leaf in the layers array. The root is computed by pairwise hashing up the binary tree from the fixed-position leaf layer.

CRITICAL OBSERVATION: recomputeDirtyFields iterates over dirtyFields in non-deterministic order, but each field update is independent (updates merkleLayers[0][fieldIndex] at a fixed position). After all dirty fields are updated, recomputeRoot rebuilds parent layers from the fixed leaf layer. Order of dirty field updates does NOT affect the final root — this is correct by design.

POTENTIAL ISSUE: If field root computation has side effects that depend on computation order (e.g., field A's root computation reads field B's shared state), non-deterministic order could cause bugs. But standard field root computation is independent.

audit_items.title: Can gossip validation produce non-deterministic outcomes for the same sidecar input?
audit_items.state_context: hasSeenDataColumnIndex checks seenDataColumnCache; setSeenDataColumnIndex is called in subscriber goroutine AFTER validation, creating a TOCTOU window

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Two genuine sources of non-determinism found: (1) KZG batch verifier timing dependency — validateWithKzgBatchVerifier submits to shared kzgChan; co-batching with concurrent invalid sidecars causes valid sidecar to fail batch verification, then fall back to slower unbatched path (different code path and latency for same valid input). (2) Non-atomic TOCTOU in seen-cache — hasSeenDataColumnIndex and setSeenDataColumnIndex operate in separate goroutine contexts (validator vs subscriber), so the same valid sidecar can produce ValidationAccept multiple times concurrently.
state_anomalies_found: TOCTOU race: hasSeenDataColumnIndex checked in validator goroutine, setSeenDataColumnIndex called in subscriber goroutine — no atomicity across the check-then-act sequence
KZG batch composition is timing-dependent: concurrent invalid sidecars can poison a valid sidecar's batch, causing it to take the unbatched fallback path
crypto/rand used for batch verifier order randomization — affects performance characteristics but not semantic outcome
Non-deterministic ValidationResult for identical input when concurrent submissions race through seen-cache check
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: seenDataColumnCache is slot-aware LRU. Get() and Add() are likely individually thread-safe but no composite transaction (check-then-set) is atomic. Two concurrent validations of the same sidecar both pass the Get() check and both proceed to ValidationAccept.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Validator goroutines run concurrently for different pubsub messages. setSeenDataColumnIndex is called from subscriber goroutine AFTER validation completes and message is forwarded. This creates a window where multiple validator goroutines for the same (slot,proposer,index) tuple can all pass the seen check and all return ValidationAccept.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Concrete race condition identified: two concurrent peers send identical sidecar. Both validator goroutines call hasSeenDataColumnIndex, both get false, both return ValidationAccept. gossipsub forwards both copies. setSeenDataColumnIndex is called twice by two subscriber goroutines. Duplicate forwarding amplifies bandwidth consumption across the mesh.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: Peer A and Peer B simultaneously send sidecar(slot=S, proposer=P, index=I). Goroutine A: hasSeenDataColumnIndex(S,P,I) → false → ValidationAccept. Goroutine B: hasSeenDataColumnIndex(S,P,I) → false → ValidationAccept (B's check completes before A's setSeenDataColumnIndex runs). Both copies forwarded to mesh peers. In 128-column PeerDAS environment, simultaneous flooding of all 128 column subnets causes up to 256x bandwidth amplification per block.
attack_scenarios: Concurrent duplicate sidecar injection from two coordinated peers causes double-forwarding through gossip mesh
128-column PeerDAS amplification: attacker floods all 128 column subnets simultaneously with duplicate sidecars to maximize bandwidth amplification

Invalid sidecar poisoning of KZG batch: attacker sends 127 invalid sidecars concurrent with 1 valid sidecar to same batch window, forcing fallback to expensive unbatched KZG verification for valid sidecar
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Race is timing-dependent: attacker must send two copies close enough in time that both hasSeenDataColumnIndex checks complete before either setSeenDataColumnIndex runs. libp2p gossipsub's concurrent message handling makes this feasible.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: validateDataColumn is directly triggered by P2P gossipsub messages on /eth2/.../data_column_sidecar_N/ssz_snappy topics. An attacker with two peers connected to the target node can trigger the race condition. Fully externally reachable.
entry_points: Any peer connected to target node
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Full P2P gossip attack surface. Any peer can send duplicate data column sidecars. Race window is small but achievable under high-concurrency conditions (e.g., block arrival time).

The same valid sidecar can produce ValidationAccept multiple times due to the non-atomic seen-cache. The KZG batch co-timing creates different code paths for the same input depending on concurrent traffic. Both sources of non-determinism are confirmed.

High slot churn: seenDataColumnCache pruning could evict recent entries, causing re-acceptance of previously-seen sidecars after slot rollover

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is the deduplication key (slot, proposer_index, sidecar.index) correctly enforced at the P2P gossip boundary?
audit_items.state_context: seenDataColumnCache is a slotAwareCache (slot-keyed LRU); setSeenDataColumnIndex called from subscriber goroutine after validation; hasSeenDataColumnIndex called from validator goroutine during gossip validation

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The deduplication key itself is correctly structured: computeCacheKey uses fmt.Sprintf('%d-%d-%d', slot, proposerIndex, index) which creates an unambiguous 3-tuple string key. No collision is possible since uint64 decimal representations are unique for different values. However, the ENFORCEMENT mechanism is architecturally broken: hasSeenDataColumnIndex (read) is called in the validator goroutine while setSeenDataColumnIndex (write) is called in the subscriber goroutine (different goroutine contexts). This creates a TOCTOU race where concurrent validators can both pass the dedup check before either subscriber marks the sidecar as seen.
state_anomalies_found: TOCTOU race: check (hasSeenDataColumnIndex) in validator goroutine, mark (setSeenDataColumnIndex) in subscriber goroutine — no atomic transaction
slotAwareCache.pruneOldestSlots removes slot metadata from slotToKeys without calling c.cache.Remove(key) on underlying LRU — data structure divergence
Correct key structure: '%d-%d-%d' is unambiguous for uint64 values — no key collision
seenDataColumnCache.Add uses slot as the first argument for slot-aware pruning — correct design but pruning bug still exists
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: slotAwareCache wraps an LRU cache with slot-based metadata for pruning. Get() checks underlying LRU. Add(slot, key, value) adds to LRU and tracks key in slotToKeys[slot] map. pruneOldestSlots removes from slotToKeys but NOT from underlying LRU — keys remain in LRU after slot pruning, causing memory leak and potentially preventing re-acceptance of future sidecars with same slot number after pruning.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Validator goroutines run concurrently. No mutex covers the validator-to-subscriber TOCTOU window. Both goroutines for identical sidecars can pass hasSeenDataColumnIndex before either setSeenDataColumnIndex runs.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Concrete TOCTOU exploit: Attacker controls two libp2p peers. Both send sidecar(slot=100, proposer=42, index=7) within the same gossip handling window. Both validator goroutines call hasSeenDataColumnIndex(100,42,7) and get false. Both return ValidationAccept. gossipsub forwards both copies. setSeenDataColumnIndex is eventually called twice (once per subscriber goroutine). Secondary: slotAwareCache pruning leaves stale LRU entries.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample:
T=0: Goroutine A calls hasSeenDataColumnIndex(100,42,7) → cache.Get('100-42-7') → false
T=1: Goroutine B calls hasSeenDataColumnIndex(100,42,7) → cache.Get('100-42-7') → false (A's Add() hasn't run yet)
T=2: Goroutine A returns ValidationAccept, gossipsub forwards copy 1
T=3: Goroutine B returns ValidationAccept, gossipsub forwards copy 2
T=4: Subscriber A calls setSeenDataColumnIndex(100,42,7) → cache.Add()
T=5: Subscriber B calls setSeenDataColumnIndex(100,42,7) → cache.Add() (redundant)
Result: Both copies forwarded to all mesh peers before dedup took effect.
attack_scenarios: Two-peer concurrent injection causes double-forwarding before dedup takes effect
In 128-column PeerDAS: flooding all 128 subnets with 2 peers each = 256 forwarded copies instead of 128
Secondary DoS: slotAwareCache pruning leak causes indefinite LRU memory growth for pruned slots
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Race window is small (milliseconds) but consistently achievable when two peers send simultaneously. Modern network conditions (co-located peers, EC2 instances) can reliably hit this window.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: hasSeenDataColumnIndex and setSeenDataColumnIndex are both triggered via P2P gossipsub message handling. Attacker needs two peers connected to the target node. No special permissions required beyond standard libp2p peer connection.
entry_points: Any libp2p peer connected to target
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Full P2P attack surface. Requires two simultaneous peer connections sending identical sidecars. Achievable with standard libp2p client.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: PROP-W2B3-25 invariant (dedup key (slot,proposer,index) enforced at P2P boundary) is NOT proven. While the key computation is correct, the enforcement mechanism is broken by the validator/subscriber goroutine split. The invariant 'each (slot,proposer,index) tuple produces at most one ValidationAccept' is violated under concurrent submission.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: computeCacheKey: correct unambiguous key; hasSeenDataColumnIndex: checks LRU cache; setSeenDataColumnIndex: marks LRU cache in subscriber goroutine
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Guard is INSUFFICIENT: no atomic transaction spanning check+mark across goroutine boundary. The guard only works for sequential (non-concurrent) inputs.
edge_cases: slotAwareCache.pruneOldestSlots removes slot metadata without removing underlying LRU entries — memory leak and potential re-acceptance after slot rollover
If seenDataColumnCache has maxSize eviction, an evicted sidecar key could be re-accepted — but maxSize is likely sufficient for practical slot windows

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Confirmed TOCTOU race condition in P2P gossip deduplication for data column sidecars. The deduplication key is correct but enforcement is split across validator and subscriber goroutines with no atomic transaction. Under concurrent submission from two peers, both receive ValidationAccept and both copies are forwarded. Additional secondary bug: slotAwareCache.pruneOldestSlots fails to remove keys from underlying LRU, causing data structure divergence. Both issues are externally reachable via P2P and attacker-controlled. Severity: High (duplicate forwarding amplification in PeerDAS network).

audit_items.title: Does the gossip network actor correctly reject duplicate data column sidecars before forwarding?
audit_items.state_context: gossipsub forwards messages to mesh peers immediately on ValidationAccept BEFORE subscriber goroutine runs. setSeenDataColumnIndex called in subscriber, not in validator. Race window between validation and subscriber allows duplicate forwarding.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The deduplication check at lines 157-159 is semantically correct per the Fulu spec ([IGNORE] dedup before forwarding). However, the check fails for concurrent submissions because: (1) gossipsub forwards messages to mesh peers immediately upon ValidationAccept return, BEFORE any subscriber callback runs; (2) setSeenDataColumnIndex is in the subscriber (called after gossipsub forwarding), not the validator. This means concurrent validators both pass the check and both trigger gossip forwarding before either marks the sidecar as seen.
state_anomalies_found: setSeenDataColumnIndex is called in subscriber goroutine AFTER gossipsub has already forwarded the message to mesh peers — the 'seen' mark is set too late to prevent duplicate forwarding
gossipsub's forward-on-accept happens synchronously within the validation call return — there is no way to prevent forwarding after returning ValidationAccept
The spec comment says [IGNORE] before forwarding, but the implementation marks seen AFTER forwarding — architectural violation of the spec intent
For duplicate detection to work, setSeenDataColumnIndex MUST be called inside validateDataColumn before returning ValidationAccept for the first acceptance
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: seenDataColumnCache is used as a best-effort dedup cache, not an authoritative mutex. It correctly prevents eventual re-acceptance of already-processed sidecars but does NOT prevent the first concurrent duplicate from being forwarded.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: The fundamental issue: gossipsub message validation and gossipsub message subscription are decoupled. Validation determines forwarding; subscription handles local processing. setSeenDataColumnIndex is called from subscription, but forwarding has already happened. Moving setSeenDataColumnIndex to validation (inside validateDataColumn, after the first acceptance) would fix the race — but introduces the inverse problem: if validation succeeds but subscription fails, the sidecar is marked seen but never processed.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Concrete forwarding amplification exploit: attacker sends N duplicate sidecars concurrently. All N validator goroutines complete hasSeenDataColumnIndex before any subscriber goroutine runs setSeenDataColumnIndex. All N return ValidationAccept. gossipsub forwards all N copies to all mesh peers. Each mesh peer repeats the same race, potentially causing network-wide amplification.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample:
T=0ms: Node receives sidecar S from peers P1, P2, P3 simultaneously
T=1ms: Three validator goroutines all call hasSeenDataColumnIndex → all get false → all return ValidationAccept
T=1ms: gossipsub forwards S×3 to all mesh peers (K neighbors in gossip mesh)
T=2ms: Three subscriber goroutines call setSeenDataColumnIndex (all succeed, last write wins)
T=2ms: K mesh peers each receive 3 copies, start 3 validator goroutines each, potentially forward 3×K copies
Total bandwidth amplification factor: up to K×(copies per node) per hop
attack_scenarios: High-concurrent duplicate injection causes multiplicative bandwidth amplification through gossip mesh hops
PeerDAS 128-column scenario: flooding all 128 subnets with 3-peer duplicate injection = 384 initial copies × K mesh factor per hop
Spec violation: the implementation violates the 'IGNORE before forwarding' intent of the spec — first acceptance always forwards, subsequent duplicates are ignored too late
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Race is consistently achievable when N peers send the same sidecar within the same gossipsub handling window (~milliseconds). Practical attack requires attacker to control N peers connected to the same target node.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: validateDataColumn is directly invoked by gossipsub's internal validator for data_column_sidecar topics. Any peer can send duplicate sidecars. The attack requires controlling multiple peer connections to the same node simultaneously.
entry_points: P2P gossipsub data_column_sidecar_N topic for N in 0..127
Any libp2p peer connected to target node
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Full P2P attack surface. Attacker needs multiple simultaneous connections (achievable with standard libp2p). Bandwidth amplification scales with mesh degree K and number of attacker-controlled peers.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: PROP-W2B3-25 invariant (duplicate sidecars rejected before forwarding) is NOT proven. The structural defect is that setSeenDataColumnIndex is called AFTER gossipsub forwarding (in subscriber), not before (in validator). The first valid occurrence of a sidecar is always forwarded (correct). Concurrent duplicates within the same validation window are also forwarded (incorrect). The invariant holds for sequential inputs but fails for concurrent inputs.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: hasSeenDataColumnIndex check in validateDataColumn at lines 157-159; pubsub.ValidationIgnore return for seen items
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Guard is INSUFFICIENT for concurrent inputs: setSeenDataColumnIndex (the write side of the guard) is called too late (post-forwarding, in subscriber goroutine). The check is in the right place but the mark is in the wrong goroutine.
edge_cases: Sequential inputs: guard works correctly — second identical sidecar is seen and returns ValidationIgnore
Concurrent inputs: guard fails — both see 'not seen' simultaneously
Fix requires moving setSeenDataColumnIndex into validateDataColumn (before ValidationAccept return) with a compare-and-swap atomic operation on the cache

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Confirmed vulnerability: the duplicate data column sidecar rejection mechanism fails for concurrent inputs because setSeenDataColumnIndex is called in the subscriber goroutine AFTER gossipsub has already forwarded the message. This is an architectural violation of the spec's [IGNORE] deduplication requirement. An attacker with multiple peer connections can inject concurrent duplicate sidecars causing forwarding amplification through the gossip mesh. In a 128-column PeerDAS network, this could cause significant bandwidth amplification. Severity: High (externally reachable, attacker-controlled, network-wide bandwidth amplification with consensus network degradation potential).
phase3_5_scope_filtering.severity_estimate: High — architectural violation of spec deduplication requirement; externally reachable forwarding amplification in PeerDAS gossip network
